topic: Serverless ClickHouse on AWS Fargate for cost‑effective analytics
postText:
You can run ClickHouse without managing servers-yes, really.

- I built a serverless pipeline where Lambda functions spin up ClickHouse containers on Fargate only when a query arrives, and results are streamed back through API Gateway. The setup uses S3 for raw logs, and Athena for ad-hoc queries that feed ClickHouse.

- Latency stayed under 200 ms for typical 1-GB scans because the cold start cost is amortized by keeping a warm pool of containers, which I tuned with provisioned concurrency. Even during peak loads, the warm pool kept response times flat, avoiding the typical Lambda cold-start spikes.

- The cost model turned out to be 30 % cheaper than a permanently-running ClickHouse on EC2 for my 50 TB/month query volume, thanks to pay-per-invocation pricing and S3 storage for data. I also enabled S3 Intelligent-Tiering for older data, pushing costs down another 5 %.

- The biggest trade-off is that complex joins across massive partitions still need careful sharding; I had to redesign my schema to favor time-series inserts and pre-aggregated tables. If you need full relational joins, consider a hybrid approach with Redshift Serverless for those rare queries.

- No patching or OS upgrades ever-updates are just new container images, which CI/CD pushes automatically. Rollbacks are as simple as swapping the image tag, so downtime is virtually zero.

Has anyone tried serverless analytics with ClickHouse? Share your findings.
